digest.component_or_area: Jira reconciler baseline advancement and three-way merge
propositions: A local status change made in the window between rebar's outbound push and the next pass's baseline advance is silently reverted by inbound if the new local value equals the pre-push baseline (ABA defect).

The baseline is advanced from the pass-START snapshot (last-fetched) rather than the last-SYNCED value, so for fields rebar itself pushed, the baseline lags by exactly one pass and the guard premise becomes false.
The inbound suppression guard (_suppressed_by_inbound) relies on `local == baseline` to mean 'local did not change', but this premise is violated for one pass after a successful outbound push.

Per-mutation success must gate baseline advancement; a soft-failed status transition (RuntimeError from illegal reverse transition) must not advance the baseline or it will falsely assert a sync that never happened.

The coverage gap: ADR 0026's mandated direction-preservation regression cell exists for title only; status and other mirrored fields were pinned against a non-production code path and never verified on the live diff_canonical_fields path.
All five inbound-mirrored fields (summary, description, priority, status, assignee) share the _suppressed_by_inbound guard and therefore share the ABA exposure and require the same fix.
